ctx.x: It didn't exist. Okay. So, I called, uh, I called Bechet and I, and he suggested Sidney D. Paris and, and Gate Mouth. And, uh, so I just made a deal with him to bring him in. And, in fact, it was Sidney who taught me the procedure. He says, well, you send us the tickets. Uh, and as soon as we get the tickets, we'll consider that a firm commitment and we'll come in, you see. So, we set the time and, uh, I got some local musicians that I already knew from Philadelphia. And so, uh, everything came together. And in…

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: And it included Sidney Bechet and Sidney D. Paris, members of Jack Teagarden's band

ctx.x: I'm beginning to get the picture on you. So you, your activities date back before being in the jazz business, date back before Journeys into Jazz? Oh yes.

My first actual public activity in jazz was when I ran a jazz concert for the American Newspaper Guild in Philadelphia at Mercantile Hall. And that was in 1936, in January of 1936. And it included Sidney Bechet and Sidney D. Paris, members of Jack Teagarden's band who were playing upstairs for dancing. That included Sterling Boze and Boze and Irving Fazola. And a local clarinet player by the name of Billy Kretschmer was there. As far as I know, this is the first actual concert ever held of authentic jazz in which…
Oh. What about, did you, did you have any trouble, uh, getting in? Have I, didn't you tell me something about that once? Are you, people didn't recognize you as the producer?
